info.description:
# Efflux Scan API

## Authentication
All endpoints require an API key passed in the `Authorization` header.

## Response Envelopes

### Single Resource — `DocumentResponse`
Endpoints that return a single resource wrap it in a `DocumentResponse`:
```json
{
"data": { ...resource fields... },
"links": {
"self": "https://api.efflux.io/v3/scans/scan_abc123"
}
}
```
The `links` map always contains `"self"`. Additional links (e.g. `"report"`, `"jobs"`) are included where applicable.

### Paginated Collection — `PagedResponse`
Endpoints that return lists use `PagedResponse`:
```json
{
"data": [ ...items... ],
"pagination": {
"limit": 20,
"page": 1,
"total": 150,
"total_pages": 8,
"has_next": true,
"has_prev": false
}
}
```
Use the `page` and `limit` query parameters to navigate pages.

### Advanced Search — `SearchPagedResponse`
Advanced search endpoints use token-based pagination:
```json
{
"data": [ ...items... ],
"pagination": {
"limit": 20,
"has_next": true,
"has_prev": false,
"next_token": "<opaque token>",
"total_count": 320,
"query": "example.com"
}
}
```
Pass the value of `next_token` as the `search_after` query parameter to retrieve the next page.

## Error Responses
All errors follow [RFC 7807 Problem Details](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807):
```json
{
"type": "https://api.efflux.io/v3/scans",
"title": "Bad Request",
"status": 400,
"detail": "target is required",
"instance": "/v3/scans"
}
```
The `type` URI links to the relevant section of this documentation. For rate-limit and
quota errors the `type` URI points to `/v3/limits`, where you can review your configured limits.
Rate-limit responses (`429`) also include a `rate_limit` extension object:
```json
{
"type": "https://api.efflux.io/v3/limits",
"title": "Rate Limit Exceeded",
"status": 429,
"detail": "rate limit exceeded",
"rate_limit": {
"limit": 60,
"remaining": 0,
"reset_at": "2026-03-13T12:00:00Z",
"retry_after": 42
}
}
```

post.description:
Creates an organization in the caller's monitoring workspace and optionally seeds initial domain and IP links in one request.

**`name`** (string, required) — display name for the monitored entity. Must be unique within the caller's tenant or solo scope.

**`domains`** (string[], optional) — domains to link immediately. Each uses **`monitoring`** plan frequencies when provided.

**`cidrs`** (string[], optional) — IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs to link immediately. Each uses **`ip_monitoring`** plan fields when provided.

At least one domain or CIDR is required. Capacity is checked against tenant-wide pools and the caller's per-user contribution limits before any records are written. On partial failure after the organization is created, created links are rolled back and the organization is soft-deleted.

Access is scoped by the authenticated session, not by query parameters. Tenant members with monitoring permission share all organizations, domain links, IP links, and delivery history within the tenant; solo users see only records they own. Plan limits are enforced against the tenant-wide pool and the caller's per-user contribution when operating in a tenant.

400.description: Invalid request or plan limit reached

409.description: Organization name, domain, or IP space already exists

post.description:
Creates a tag-only matching rule applied to scan and URL funnel results for the authenticated user or tenant.

### Matching
Queries are evaluated with OR semantics unless `run_all_queries` is true, in which case every matching query contributes tags.
Within a single query, all fields, headers, and cookies must match (AND).

### Field precisions
`eq`, `lazy`, `contains`, `lazy_contains`, `regex` (RE2), and `in` are supported on rule fields.
Regex patterns are validated at create/update time and matched in-memory (not via MongoDB).

### Tags
At least one tag must be present on the rule or on a query.

Explains which fields matched for a saved rule (`rule_id`) or draft `queries` against one scan, URL, or DNS result.
Returns a MatchReport with hit spans for UI highlighting. Does not persist anything.

post.description:
Creates and starts a new scan job based on the provided parameters. The body of the request defines the targets, scan options, and optional webhook callbacks.

### Scan Parameters
---
**`hosts`** (array of strings)
A list of targets. Accepts single IPs, CIDR blocks, or the name of a custom host list.
```json
"hosts": ["1.2.3.4", "10.0.0.0/24", "my_internal_servers"]
```

**`ports`** (array of strings)
A list of ports to scan. Accepts single ports, ranges, 'top_#' lists, or the name of a custom port list.
```json
"ports": ["22", "80-88", "top_1000", "my_common_ports"]
```

**`proto`** (string)
The protocol for the port scan.
- `"tcp"` (default)
- `"udp"`

**`fingerprint`** (boolean)
Enables service and version fingerprinting on open ports.
- `false` (default): Fast check to see if a port is open.
- `true`: Slower, more detailed check to identify the running service.
> **Note:** Setting `fingerprint: true` doubles the request count: `(hosts * ports) * 2`.

**`checks`** (boolean)
Enables the vulnerability checking system.
- `false` (default): Vulnerability checks are disabled.
- `true`: Vulnerability checks are enabled.
> **Note:** Enabling `checks` can significantly increase scan duration.

**`checks_options`** (object)
Options for the vulnerability checks.
```json
"checks_options": { "cves_only": false, "min_severity": "high" }
```

**`collect`** (object)
Bypasses fingerprinting and attempts to collect data from specified services on given ports.
```json
"collect": { "ssh": ["22", "2222"], "rdp": ["3389"] }
```

**`tags`** (array of strings)
A list of tags to add to the job.
Max of 10 tags, each tag can be up to 40 characters long.
```json
"tags": ["web", "security"]
```

**`description`** (string)
Max of 300 characters.
A description of the job.
```json
"description": "This is a job to scan the web for vulnerabilities"
```

### Web & CVE Parameters
---
These parameters modify the scan behavior for web asset discovery or targeted CVE checks.

**`domains`** (array of strings): A list of domain names to include in the scan.
**`urls`** (array of strings): A list of specific URLs to target.
**`paths`** (array of strings): A list of paths to append to hosts and domains for HTTP collection.
**`paths_https`** (boolean): If `true`, forces HTTPS for all path-based collection.
**`cves`** (array of strings): A list of specific CVEs to check for.

> **⚠️ Important Exclusivity Rules:**
> - **Using `cves`**: You cannot use `urls` or `paths`. Hosts and domains will only be used as targets for the specified CVE checks, disabling normal scanning.
> - **Using `urls` or `paths`**: You cannot use `cves`. Hosts and domains will only be used as targets for HTTP collection, disabling normal port scanning and lookups.

### Webhook Callbacks
---
Configure webhook callbacks for job lifecycle events. The `$job_id` variable in URLs will be replaced with the job's ID.

- **`start_url`**, **`start_method`**: Called when the job starts.
- **`success_url`**, **`success_method`**: Called when the job completes successfully.
- **`fail_url`**, **`fail_method`**: Called when the job fails. *(Not yet implemented)*
- **`summary_only`** (boolean): If `true`, the callback payload will omit the full results.

Methods can be `POST` (default) or `GET`. The `efflux-job-id` header is included in all callback requests.

post.description:
Creates and starts a new schedule based on the provided parameters. The body of the request defines the schedule details, including the frequency, time configuration, and task details.

### Schedule Parameters
---
**`name`** (string)
The name of the schedule.
```json
"name": "My Schedule"
```
**`description`** (string)
The description of the schedule.
```json
"description": "This is a schedule description."
```
**`frequency`** (string)
The frequency of the schedule.
```json
"frequency": "daily"
```
**`minute`** (int)
The minute of the hour to run the schedule.
```json
"minute": 30
```
**`hour`** (int)
The hour of the day to run the schedule.
For daily, weekly, and monthly schedules, this field is required (0-23).
For multi-hour schedules (every_2_hours, every_3_hours, etc.), this field is optional and specifies the offset within the interval:
- every_2_hours: hour must be 0-1 (e.g., hour=1 runs at 01:mm, 03:mm, 05:mm, etc.)
- every_3_hours: hour must be 0-2 (e.g., hour=2 runs at 02:mm, 05:mm, 08:mm, etc.)
- every_4_hours: hour must be 0-3 (e.g., hour=1 runs at 01:mm, 05:mm, 09:mm, etc.)
- every_6_hours: hour must be 0-5
- every_8_hours: hour must be 0-7
- every_12_hours: hour must be 0-11
```json
"hour": 12
```
**`day_of_week`** (int)
The day of the week to run the schedule.
```json
"day_of_week": 0
```
**`day_of_month`** (int)
The day of the month to run the schedule.
```json
"day_of_month": 15
```
**`run_until`** (string)
The date and time to run the schedule until.
```json
"run_until": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```
If the schedule contains a domain survey task, it must be set to a frequency of weekly or longer.
If the schedule contains a capture task, it must be set to a frequency of daily or longer.
If the schedule contains a permutation check task, it must be set to a frequency of daily or longer.

get.description:
Performs linguistic full-text search across DNS result fields with BM25 relevance scoring.

**Search Features:**
- Full-text search with stemming and linguistic analysis
- BM25 relevance scoring (results ordered by relevance)
- Cursor-based pagination with O(1) performance

**Query Examples:**
- `?q=cloudflare google` - Find results containing cloudflare OR google
- `?q=\"exact phrase\"` - Find exact phrase matches
- `?q=nameserver&fields=ns,txt` - Search specific fields only

**Pagination:**
- `?limit=50` - Results per page (default: 20, max: 100)
- `?search_after=TOKEN` - Get next page using token from previous response
- Tokens are base64-encoded strings for efficient cursor pagination

**Filters (combine with full-text search):**
- `?domain=example.com` - Filter by exact domain
- `?min_date=2024-01-01` - Filter by minimum checked_at date (ISO 8601 format)

**Response includes:**
- `score` - BM25 relevance score (higher = more relevant)
- `next_token` - Base64-encoded pagination token (string)
- `has_next` - Whether more results are available
- `total_count` - Estimated total matching documents (approximate)
get.summary: Full-text search DNS results

Performs linguistic full-text search across URL result fields with BM25 relevance scoring.

**Search Features:**
- Full-text search with stemming and linguistic analysis
- Typo tolerance with fuzzy matching
- BM25 relevance scoring (results ordered by relevance)
- Efficient cursor-based pagination (O(1) performance)

**Query Examples:**
- `?q=wordpress admin` - Find URL results containing wordpress OR admin
- `?q="exact phrase"` - Find exact phrase matches
- `?q=jquery&fields=script_urls,raw` - Search specific fields only

**Pagination:**
- `?limit=50` - Results per page (default: 20, max: 100)
- `?search_after=TOKEN` - Get next page using token from previous response
- Tokens are base64-encoded strings for efficient cursor pagination

**Filters (combine with full-text search):**
- `?domain=example.com` - Filter by domain
- `?status_code=200` - Filter by HTTP status code
- `?min_date=2024-01-01` - Filter by minimum date (ISO 8601 format)

**Response includes:**
- `score` - BM25 relevance score (higher = more relevant)
- `next_token` - Base64-encoded pagination token (string)
- `has_next` - Whether more results are available
- `total_count` - Estimated total matching documents (approximate)

get.description:
Opens a WebSocket for live scan results across all jobs you can access.

**Connect** — `wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/scans`

**Authentication** — `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, <token>`

**Command-line example:**
`websocat -t -k 'wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/scans' -H="Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, ${TOKEN}"`

**After connect** — `connected` message, then live envelopes (`scan`, `dns`, `url`, `check`). Live-only; use `GET /scans/{job_id}/results` for history.

**Raw payloads** — scan and url `raw` fields are omitted by default. Pass `raw_limit=N` to include raw strings truncated to N bytes each (capped at the server maximum).
get.summary: Stream live scan results (all jobs)

parameters.description: Filter to a tenant member's jobs
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: Max bytes per raw string in scan/url results; omit raw when unset or 0; capped at server max
parameters.name: raw_limit

parameters.description: Browser origin; not required for non-browser clients
parameters.name: Origin

403.description: Insufficient permissions or origin not allowed

get.description:
Opens a WebSocket for live scan results for one job. Same auth and keepalive as `/stream/scans`.

**Connect** — `wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/scans/{job_id}`

**Authentication** — `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, <token>`

**Command-line example:**
`websocat -t -k 'wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/scans/{job_id}' -H="Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, ${TOKEN}"`

**Tenant scope** — callers with `scans:read_tenant` (or `tenant_admin`) automatically
stream any job in their tenant. Optional `tenant_view=true` remains valid for list streams.

**Raw payloads** — scan and url `raw` fields are omitted by default. Pass `raw_limit=N` to include raw strings truncated to N bytes each (capped at the server maximum).
get.summary: Stream live scan results (single job)

parameters.description: Optional; by-id streams auto-elevate when caller has tenant read privileges
parameters.name: tenant_view

parameters.description: Max bytes per raw string in scan/url results; omit raw when unset or 0; capped at server max
parameters.name: raw_limit

parameters.description: Browser origin; not required for non-browser clients
parameters.name: Origin

403.description: Insufficient permissions or origin not allowed

404.description: Job not found or not accessible

get.description:
Opens a WebSocket for live status changes (jobs, captures, tasks, surveys, permutations).

**Connect** — `wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/status`

**Authentication** — `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, <token>`

**Command-line example:**
`websocat -t -k 'wss://api.efflux.io/v3/stream/status' -H="Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: efflux.v1, ${TOKEN}"`

**Filter by type** — optional `type=job,capture` (aliases: `scan` → `job`). Omit to receive all types.
get.summary: Stream live resource status changes

status.description:
Status is the status of the capture request
pending: waiting for the capture to be attempted
captured: capture was attempted and succeeded

attempted_at.description: CapturedAt is the time the capture was attempted

deleted.description: ImageDeleted is true if the user has marked the capture image for deletion

capture_id.description: CaptureRequestID is the unique identifier for the capture request that created this capture

url.description: URL is the URL the capture is for

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the time the capture was created

decoded_value.description:
DecodedValue holds the deepest human-readable decoded form of the cookie
value after URL and base64 decoding.

captured_domains.description: CapturedDomains holds a list of all domains found while working this domain and its subdomains

a_record_for.description: ARecordFor holds a list of all domains for which this host is an A record

domain.description: Domain is the domain we are surveying

tracked_subdomains.description: TrackedSubdomains is a list of subdomains we want to track for this domain, copied from the 'SurveySchedule'. We will always do lookups for these subdomains

sct_logged_at.description: SCTLoggedAt is this leaf’s CT SignedCertificateTimestamp time (RFC3339Nano UTC), when present.

ping_responded.description:
PingResponded is true when the server responded to any of our CoAP requests,
including an explicit RST to a CoAP Ping (empty CON, RFC 7252 §4.2) or
any ACK to GET /.well-known/core.  Acts as the general "CoAP confirmed" flag.

csm_received.description:
CSMReceived is true when the server sent a Capabilities and Settings Message
(Code 7.01) immediately after the TCP/TLS connection was established.
Present only for TCP/TLS transport (RFC 8323 §5.3).

max_message_size.description:
MaxMessageSize is the maximum receive buffer the server advertised in its
CSM frame (TCP only).  Zero when the option was absent or not applicable.

block_wise.description:
BlockWise is true when the server's CSM includes the Block-Wise Transfer
Supported option (TCP only, RFC 8323 §5.3.2).

core_payload.description:
CorePayload is the raw application/link-format body from GET /.well-known/core
(RFC 6690).  Contains comma-separated URI references with resource attributes.
Empty when the resource is absent, protected, or no payload was returned.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer is the device manufacturer string from LwM2M /3/0/0.

model_number.description: ModelNumber is the device model string from LwM2M /3/0/1.

serial_number.description: SerialNumber is the device serial number string from LwM2M /3/0/2.

firmware_version.description: FirmwareVersion is the firmware revision string from LwM2M /3/0/3.

iin1.description: IIN status bytes from first response or unsolicited frame.

group0_unsupported.description: True when Group 0 queries returned IIN2.1 (Object Unknown).

class0_responded.description: True when fallback Class 0 integrity poll received any data.

client_node.description:
Node Address Exchange (phase 1).
ClientNode is a pointer so that an explicitly assigned node 0 (a valid
auto-assigned value) is distinguishable from "exchange never completed"
(nil, omitted by omitempty).

udp_port.description:
Pointer so that an explicitly returned port of 0 ("no UDP port configured")
is distinguishable from "Info Read was never completed" (nil).

manufacturer_id.description: Device identity (from Command 0 — Read Unique Identifier).

tag.description: Asset identification (from Command 13 — Read Tag, Descriptor, Date).

tags.description: Tags is gathered from the scan results

ports.description: Ports maps the port number to the scan result for that port

checks.description: Checks will be mapped by host here

vendor_name.description:
VendorName is the value of the vendorName RootDSE attribute (RFC 3045).
Examples: "Apache Software Foundation", "389 Project", "Ping Identity".
Microsoft Active Directory does not expose this attribute.

vendor_version.description:
VendorVersion is the value of the vendorVersion RootDSE attribute
(RFC 3045).  Examples: "389-Directory/2.3.1", "Apache Directory Server".

default_naming_context.description:
DefaultNamingContext is the primary directory partition (AD-specific).
Format: "DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com" — identifies the hosted domain.

root_domain_naming_context.description:
RootDomainNamingContext is the forest root partition (AD-specific).
Differs from DefaultNamingContext on child domains in a multi-domain forest.

naming_contexts.description:
NamingContexts lists all directory partitions hosted by this DSA.
Typical content: one or more "DC=..." entries plus config/schema partitions.

dns_host_name.description:
DnsHostName is the fully qualified DNS hostname of the server (AD-specific).
Example: "dc01.corp.example.com"

server_name.description:
ServerName is the LDAP DN of the server's NTDS Settings object (AD-specific).
Encodes the site and server name.
Example: "CN=NTDS Settings,CN=DC01,CN=Servers,CN=Default-First-Site-Name,..."

supported_ldap_versions.description:
SupportedLDAPVersions lists protocol versions the server will accept.
Typical values: ["3"] or ["2","3"].

supported_sasl_mechanisms.description:
SupportedSASLMechanisms lists the SASL authentication schemes the server
advertises.  Examples: "GSSAPI", "NTLM", "EXTERNAL", "PLAIN".
Note: we never invoke any of these — this is read-only RootDSE enumeration.

subschema_subentry.description:
SubschemaSubentry is the DN of the server's schema entry.
OpenLDAP uses "cn=Subschema"; AD uses "CN=Aggregate,...".

config_context.description:
ConfigContext is the DN of the server's configuration partition.
OpenLDAP: "cn=config"; AD: "CN=Configuration,DC=...".

forest_functionality.description:
ForestFunctionality is the functional level of the AD forest (AD-specific).
Integer string: "7" = Windows Server 2016+, "6" = 2012 R2, etc.

domain_functionality.description: DomainFunctionality is the functional level of the AD domain (AD-specific).

is_global_catalog_ready.description:
IsGlobalCatalogReady indicates the server is a Global Catalog replica.
Sourced from the isGlobalCatalogReady RootDSE attribute (AD-specific).

server_type.description:
ServerType is inferred from the combination of observed RootDSE attributes.
Possible values: "ActiveDirectory", "OpenLDAP", "389DS", "ApacheDS",
"eDirectory", "DomainController", "LDAP".

result_code.description:
ResultCode is the LDAP result code from the SearchResultDone message.
0 = success; 1 = operationsError; 32 = noSuchObject;
48 = inappropriateAuthentication; 50 = insufficientAccessRights.
Pointer so that a successful result code of 0 is distinguishable from
"SearchResultDone was never received" (nil, omitted by omitempty).

service_types.description:
ServiceTypes lists all advertised DNS-SD service types discovered from a
_services._dns-sd._udp.local. PTR query (RFC 6763 §9).
Values are dot-separated service-type strings, e.g. "_http._tcp" or "_ssh._tcp".

model.description:
Model is the hardware model identifier string from the TXT record model= key
in a _device-info._tcp.local. response (e.g., "Macmini8,1", "J105aA").

ty.description:
Ty is the human-readable device display title from the TXT ty= key
(e.g., "HP LaserJet 1200", "AirPort Express").

osx_vers.description: OsxVers is the OS or kernel major version string from the TXT osxvers= key.

md.description:
Md is the device model string from the TXT md= key, common in embedded IoT
and home-automation daemons (e.g., "Chromecast Audio", "Google Home Mini").

usb_mfg.description: UsbMfg is the USB manufacturer string from the TXT usb_MFG= key.

usb_mdl.description: UsbMdl is the USB device model string from the TXT usb_MDL= key.

cpu_model_name.description:
CPU Type Read (command 0101h, subcommand 0000h).
Returns 16-byte ASCII model name and 2-byte numeric model code.

sd_error_code.description:
Batch Read SD0 (command 0401h, subcommand 0000h, device SD, address 0, 1 word).
SD0 = Latest Self-Diagnostic Error code; 0x0000 = no error.
Pointer so that a healthy value of 0 is distinguishable from "batch read
was never attempted" (nil, omitted by omitempty).

scan_time_current.description:
Batch Read SD200–SD201 (device SD, address 200, 2 words; units: 0.1 ms).
SD200 = current scan time; SD201 = maximum scan time since last reset.

protocol_version.description:
Protocol level that produced the CONNACK.
4 = MQTT v3.1.1 (Protocol Level 4).
5 = MQTT v5.0  (Protocol Level 5).

connack_code.description:
CONNACK return code byte.
0x00 Accepted.
0x01 Unsupported Protocol Version (v3.1.1 rejected; v5.0 attempted).
0x02 Identifier Rejected (zero-length Client IDs disabled).
0x03 Server Unavailable.
0x04 Bad User Name or Password (credentials required).
0x05 Not Authorized (ACL / IP filter blocked).

connack_accepted.description: True when the broker accepted the connection without credentials (code 0x00).

broker_version.description:
Broker software and version from $SYS/broker/version.
Example: "mosquitto version 2.0.18", "emqx 5.3.0", "HiveMQ 4.20.0".

uptime.description:
Broker uptime string from $SYS/broker/uptime.
Example: "12345 seconds".

clients_total.description: Total client connections since broker start from $SYS/broker/clients/total.

messages_stored.description: Retained messages in broker storage from $SYS/broker/messages/stored.

messages_sent.description: Total messages sent by broker from $SYS/broker/messages/sent.

ping_responded.description: True when broker replied to PINGREQ with PINGRESP.

ntp_version.description:
NtpVersion is the NTP protocol version reported in the Mode 4 response
(bits 5–3 of byte 0), or from Mode 6 version= when it is a bare digit.
Common values: 3 (NTPv3) or 4 (NTPv4).

stratum.description:
Stratum is the clock stratum from the Mode 4 response (byte 1).
  1 = primary reference clock (directly attached GPS, PPS, etc.).
  2–15 = secondary server synchronized to a stratum N-1 server.
  0 or 16 = unspecified / unsynchronized.

leap_indicator.description:
LeapIndicator is the 2-bit leap second warning from byte 0 of the
Mode 4 response (or Mode 6 leap=).  0=no warning, 1=+1 s at end of day,
2=−1 s, 3=alarm.

ref_id.description:
RefID is the Reference Identifier from bytes 12–15 of the Mode 4 response
(or Mode 6 refid=). For stratum 1 servers it is a 4-character ASCII clock
source code (e.g., "GPS", "PPS", "CDMA", "WWVB", "DCF", "ATOM").
For stratum 2+ it is the IPv4 address of the upstream reference server.

daemon_version.description:
DaemonVersion is the full version string from the Mode 6 readvar payload
when version="…" carries a daemon build string.
Format: "ntpd <semver>@<hash>-o <build_info>"
Example: "ntpd 4.2.8p15@1.3728-o Mon Jan 7 09:12:01 UTC 2019 (1)"

processor.description:
Processor is the CPU architecture string from the Mode 6 readvar payload.
Examples: "x86_64", "aarch64", "armv7l", "mips", "powerpc", "unknown".

system.description:
System is the OS/kernel string from the Mode 6 readvar payload.
Format: "<OS>/<kernel-release>" or "<Vendor>/<Product>"
Examples: "Linux/5.10.0-21-amd64", "FreeBSD/13.2-RELEASE", "UNIX", "Cisco/IOS".

precision.description:
Precision is Mode 6 precision= (log2 seconds of local clock resolution).
Typical values are negative (e.g. -10 ≈ 1 ms, -20 ≈ 1 µs).

root_delay.description:
RootDelay is Mode 6 rootdelay= (total round-trip delay to the primary
reference), preserved as the ASCII decimal from the daemon.

root_dispersion.description:
RootDispersion is Mode 6 rootdispersion= (total dispersion to the
primary reference), preserved as ASCII decimal.

peer.description: Peer is Mode 6 peer= — association ID of the current system peer.

ref_time.description: RefTime is Mode 6 reftime= (reference timestamp, often 0xXXXXXXXX.XXXXXXXX).

poll.description: Poll is Mode 6 poll= (log2 seconds of the poll interval).

clock.description: Clock is Mode 6 clock= (local clock timestamp string).

state.description: State is Mode 6 state= — ntpd clock-state / discipline FSM code.

offset.description: Offset is Mode 6 offset= (local clock offset vs peer), ASCII decimal.

frequency.description: Frequency is Mode 6 frequency= (frequency offset in ppm), ASCII decimal.

jitter.description: Jitter is Mode 6 jitter=, ASCII decimal.

noise.description: Noise is Mode 6 noise=, ASCII decimal.

stability.description: Stability is Mode 6 stability=, ASCII decimal.

mode6_restricted.description:
Mode6Restricted is true when the NTP daemon replied to the Mode 6 probe
with an error bit set (E=1), indicating `restrict noquery` is configured.
NTP daemon presence is confirmed even when this is true.

transport_error_code.description: ERR response fields (present when server replied with ERRF instead of ACKF).

security_policy_uri.description: Endpoint security profile (from GetEndpoints, first endpoint).

context_accepted.description:
ContextAccepted is true when the Bind_Ack result code was 0x0000
(acceptance), confirming the remote host runs PNIO-CM.
A Bind_Ack received on port 34964 is itself strong evidence of PROFINET.

assoc_group_id.description:
AssocGroupID is the server-assigned association group from the Bind_Ack.
Non-zero when the DCE/RPC session was established.

vendor_id.description:
VendorID from I&M0 byte offset 6 (big-endian uint16).
Common values: 0x002A = Siemens, 0x001A = ABB, 0x00B0 = Phoenix Contact,
               0x0196 = Beckhoff, 0x016A = Belden, 0x012D = Wago.

vendor_name.description:
VendorName is the human-readable name mapped from VendorID.
Empty when the VendorID is not in the well-known lookup table.

order_id.description:
OrderID is the 20-character part number from I&M0 offset 8.
Example: "6ES7 515-2AM01-0AB0".

serial_number.description: SerialNumber is the 16-character serial from I&M0 offset 28.

software_revision.description:
SoftwareRevision is formatted as "[Prefix][Major].[Minor].[Build]".
Prefix codes: V=released, R=revision, P=prototype, U=under test, T=test.
Example: "V2.1.0".

profile_id.description:
ProfileID from I&M0 offset 52.
Example: 0x3A00 = PROFIdrive, 0xF600 = Generic Device.

im_supported.description:
IMSupported bitmask from I&M0 offset 58 indicating which optional
I&M records (I&M1–I&M4) the device supports.
Bit 0 = I&M1, Bit 1 = I&M2, Bit 2 = I&M3, Bit 3 = I&M4.

ptp_version.description:
PtpVersion is the PTP protocol version from byte 1 of the response header.
Value 2 indicates IEEE 1588-2008 or IEEE 1588-2019.

domain.description:
Domain is the PTP domain number (byte 4 of the response header).
Default domain = 0.  Industrial deployments may use domains 0–127.

clock_id.description:
ClockID is the 8-byte EUI-64 clock identity of the responding device,
hex-encoded as a 16-character string (e.g., "0C0C3AFFFE1B4D00").
Derived from bytes 20–27 of the Management response header.

clock_type.description:
ClockType is a human-readable string decoded from the 16-bit clockType
bitmask in the CLOCK_DESCRIPTION TLV.
Values: "Ordinary Clock", "Boundary Clock", "End-to-End Transparent Clock",
         "Peer-to-Peer Transparent Clock", or a hex string for unknown masks.

manufacturer_oui.description:
ManufacturerOUI is the 3-byte IEEE OUI extracted from the manufacturerIdentity
field in the CLOCK_DESCRIPTION TLV, formatted as "XX:XX:XX" (hex, uppercase).
Well-known OUIs: 00:0C:42 (Meinberg), 00:1E:C0 (Symmetricom),
                 00:1A:A0 (Microsemi), 00:A0:69 (Cisco Timing),
                 00:06:55 (Endrun Technologies).

product_description.description:
ProductDescription is the PTPtext productDescription string from the
CLOCK_DESCRIPTION TLV.  Contains the model name and hardware revision.
Example: "LANTIME M1000/GNSS; R1234; HW2"

revision_data.description:
RevisionData is the PTPtext revisionData string from the CLOCK_DESCRIPTION TLV.
Contains the active firmware version and software build information.
Example: "7.02.006; 2023-11-15"

user_description.description:
UserDescription is the PTPtext userDescription string from the
CLOCK_DESCRIPTION TLV.  An administrator-defined label for the device,
often the hostname or physical rack/site designation.

clock_class.description:
ClockClass is the clockQuality.clockClass value from DEFAULT_DATA_SET.
6 = primary reference; 135 = holdover (acceptable); 187 = out-of-spec.
Lower values indicate better clock quality.

server.description:
Server is the Server: header from the OPTIONS 200 OK response.
E.g., "Hikvision-RTSP/1.0", "Axis/1.0", "VLC/3.0.18", "DSS/6.0.3".

public_methods.description:
PublicMethods lists the RTSP methods from the Public: header.
Presence of SETUP, TEARDOWN, or PLAY uniquely identifies an RTSP streaming stack.

auth_required.description:
AuthRequired is true when the server returned 401 Unauthorized.
This confirms an active RTSP daemon even when credentials are unknown.

www_authenticate.description:
WwwAuthenticate is the WWW-Authenticate: header value from the 401 response.
E.g., "Digest realm=\"IP Camera\", nonce=\"a3f78b19\"".

session_name.description:
SessionName is the s= field from the SDP payload in the DESCRIBE response.
E.g., "Media Presentation", "Camera Stream", "Live Stream".

video_codec.description:
VideoCodec is the primary video codec name from the SDP (from a=rtpmap or
static payload type assignment).  E.g., "H264", "H265", "JPEG", "MPV".

audio_codec.description:
AudioCodec is the primary audio codec name from the SDP.
E.g., "PCMU", "PCMA", "AAC", "G722".

sdp.description: Sdp is the raw SDP body from the DESCRIBE 200 OK response (capped at 8 KB).

version.description:
Version is the highest SNMP version that responded ("v1", "v2c", "v3").
Determined by the first version-specific probe that elicited a response.

community.description:
Community is the SNMP community string that elicited a read response.
Typically "public" for unauthenticated read-only access.

sys_descr.description:
SysDescr is the sysDescr.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0).
Full-text description of the entity: OS name, hardware platform, software
version, and build/compilation timestamp.  E.g.:
  "Linux 5.15.0-88-generic #98-Ubuntu SMP x86_64"
  "Cisco IOS Software, Version 15.2(7)E4, RELEASE SOFTWARE"

sys_object_id.description:
SysObjectID is the sysObjectID.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0).
An OID that points to the vendor's private enterprise MIB subtree.
E.g., "1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.1042" (Cisco Catalyst 3750).

sys_up_time.description:
SysUpTime is the sysUpTime.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0) in hundredths
of seconds since the network management subsystem was last re-initialized.
ASN.1 type TimeTicks (tag 0x43).

sys_contact.description:
SysContact is the sysContact.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.4.0).
System administrator contact information (free-form text or email).

sys_name.description:
SysName is the sysName.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0).
The Fully Qualified Domain Name or administrative hostname of the entity.

sys_location.description:
SysLocation is the sysLocation.0 value (OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.6.0).
Physical location of the entity (rack position, site name, city, etc.).

engine_id.description:
EngineID is the hex-encoded SNMPv3 authoritative engine ID extracted from
the unauthenticated SNMPv3 Engine ID Discovery Report-PDU response.
Format: RFC 3411 §5 (first 4 bytes encode enterprise number with high-bit).

enterprise.description:
Enterprise is the IANA Private Enterprise Number (PEN) decoded from the
first 4 bytes of the engine ID (RFC 3411 §5).
Well-known values: 9=Cisco, 2636=Juniper, 311=Microsoft, 2011=Huawei,
4874=Juniper (alt), 8072=net-snmp, 12356=Fortinet, 14823=Aruba.

server.description:
Server is the SERVER header from the SSDP 200 OK response.
Format: OS/Version UPnP/Version Product/Version.
E.g., "Linux/3.10.14 UPnP/1.0 Portable SDK for UPnP devices/1.6.19".

location.description: Location is the LOCATION header URL pointing to the XML Device Description Document.

usn.description:
USN is the Unique Service Name from the USN header.
E.g., "uuid:f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6::upnp:rootdevice".

st.description: ST is the Search Target echoed in the 200 OK response (e.g., "upnp:rootdevice").

friendly_name.description: FriendlyName is the <friendlyName> element — human-readable device label.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer is the <manufacturer> element — device vendor/brand.

model_name.description: ModelName is the <modelName> element — product model descriptor.

model_number.description: ModelNumber is the <modelNumber> element — hardware revision or SKU.

model_description.description: ModelDescription is the <modelDescription> element — capability profile string.

device_type.description:
DeviceType is the <deviceType> element — standardized UPnP Forum URN.
E.g., "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1".

firmware_version.description: FirmwareVersion is the <firmwareVersion> element — operational build identifier.

serial_number.description: SerialNumber is the <serialNumber> element — hardware serial number.

transport.description:
Transport is the confirmed syslog transport:
"tcp" (plain TCP 514), "tls" (RFC 5425 TLS 6514), or "beep" (RFC 3195).

message_accepted.description:
MessageAccepted is true when the server accepted our RFC 5424 syslog
message without an immediate RST, FIN, or error response.
Confirms an active syslog collector is listening on the port.

beep_profiles.description:
BEEPProfiles lists the profile URIs advertised in the BEEP greeting
(RFC 3080 §2.3.1.3).  Present only for port 601 (BEEP transport).
Standard syslog profiles:
  "http://iana.org/beep/syslog/RAW"    — RFC 3195 RAW profile
  "http://iana.org/beep/syslog/COOKED" — RFC 3195 COOKED profile

beep_server_state.description:
BEEPServerState is the raw XML content of the BEEP greeting body
(trimmed), useful for debugging non-standard implementations.

start_dt_confirmed.description: STARTDT CON received — session is in STARTED state.

end_of_init_received.description:
End of Initialization (M_EI_NA_1, TypeID 70) received spontaneously.
Indicates the device rebooted or was reset.  COI byte encodes restart cause.

single_point_count.description:
Data point counts from General Interrogation (COT=20).
All TypeID variants (with and without CP56Time2a timestamp) are aggregated.

interrogation_complete.description: True when the outstation sent C_IC_NA_1 with COT=10 (Activation Termination).

counter_interrogation_complete.description:
Counter Interrogation (C_CI_NA_1, Type ID 101) result.
QCC=0x05 = General counter group, No Freeze, No Reset — fully read-only.
CounterCount is the total number of integrated total objects returned.

device_time.description:
Device clock from Clock Synchronization Read (C_CS_NA_1, TypeID 103, COT=5).
Formatted as RFC3339 UTC.  Empty if device did not respond or clock is invalid.

transport.description: Transport is the confirmed WinRM transport: "http" (5985) or "https" (5986).

http_status.description:
HTTPStatus is the HTTP status code returned by the Identify request.
200 = full identify data available; 401 = auth required.

protocol_version.description:
ProtocolVersion is the DMTF WS-Management protocol version URI.
Typically "http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman.xsd".

product_vendor.description:
ProductVendor identifies the WinRM stack implementation.
Microsoft Windows returns "Microsoft Corporation".
Linux implementations return "Openwsman Project" or a vendor OEM string.

product_version.description:
ProductVersion is the raw version string from the IdentifyResponse.
Format for Microsoft endpoints: "OS: <build> SP: <sp> Stack: <stack>"
e.g. "OS: 6.3.9600 SP: 0.0 Stack: 3.0"
Unauthenticated responses obscure the OS build with "OS: 0.0.0".

os_version.description:
OSVersion is the OS build extracted from ProductVersion.
e.g. "6.3.9600" maps to Windows Server 2012 R2 / Windows 8.1.
"10.0.x" maps to Windows Server 2016/2019/2022 or Windows 10/11.

service_pack.description: ServicePack is the SP version extracted from ProductVersion.

stack_version.description: StackVersion is the WS-Management engine stack version.

security_profiles.description:
SecurityProfiles lists the security profile URIs advertised in the
IdentifyResponse, e.g.:
  "http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman/secprofile/http/basic"
  "http://schemas.dmtf.org/wbem/wsman/1/wsman/secprofile/http/spnego-kerberos"

auth_methods.description:
AuthMethods lists authentication schemes advertised via WWW-Authenticate
response headers (present only when HTTPStatus == 401).
e.g. ["Negotiate", "Kerberos", "NTLM", "Basic"].

server_header.description:
ServerHeader is the raw HTTP Server header from the WinRM response.
Microsoft HTTP.sys returns "Microsoft-HTTPAPI/<version>".

any_val.description:
AnyVal tells us we only need to check for the presence of a matching header key
if AnyVal is true, we don't check Value

any_name.description: AnyName tells us to accept any header name and check for value matches

start_index.description: byte offset into MatchedText; -1 if N/A

fields.description: Fields holds any field that doesn't require special handling (like headers or cookies)

tags.description:
Tags are tags to add to the result if this particular query is the one that matched - This can be in addition to, or instead of, the 'tags' field at the top level of a rule
It is useful for combining multiple different tagging queries into a single rule.

scan.description: --- Task Details (only one should be set) ---
